line: When the chest is tight and tomorrow won't sit still

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ
dua.body: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from the burden of debt and from being overpowered by men. The Prophet ﷺ used to say this.

items.title: Anxiety and the Reframing of Ta'weel
items.why: A reflection for the 3am ceiling

items.title: The Morsel of Flesh
items.why: The hadith on the heart: when it is sound, the whole body is sound

items.title: Ayyub — The Patient One
items.why: His dua in deep affliction: 'You are the Most Merciful of the merciful' (21:83)

line: When something or someone is gone

dua.arabic: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ، اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي وَاخْلُفْ لِي خَيْرًا مِنْهَا
dua.body: Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return. O Allah, reward me in my affliction and give me something better than it in exchange. The Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever says this when struck by a calamity, Allah gives them something better.

items.title: The Grammar of Loss
items.why: The words to say when loss strikes (2:156)

items.title: Umm Salama — The Dua and What Followed
items.why: She said this dua after Abu Salama died (Muslim 918)

items.title: The Beautiful Patience
items.why: Ya'qub's grief for Yusuf: 'patience is most fitting' (12:18), and no despair of relief (12:87)

line: When the heat rises and the tongue loads

dua.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
dua.body: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. The Prophet ﷺ said this word relaxes a man in anger (Bukhari 3282). He also said: if one of you is angry while standing, let him sit; if the anger leaves, good, and if not, let him lie down (Abu Dawud 4782: sahih per al-Albani and Darussalam).
dua.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 3282; Sunan Abi Dawud 4782 (sahih per al-Albani; sahih per Darussalam)

items.title: Yusuf — 'No Blame Upon You'
items.why: The grudge that melted into 'No blame will there be upon you today' (12:92)

items.title: Play 5: Anger & Argument
items.why: Repel evil with what is better (41:34); the strong one controls himself in anger

items.title: The Two Rivers of Ibrahim
items.why: He answered his people's fire with reason, not rage (21:51-70)

line: When the crowd is full and the room is empty

dua.arabic: وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ ۚ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ
dua.body: And He is with you wherever you are. And We are closer to him than his jugular vein.

items.title: Loneliness in the Crowd
items.why: A crowded feed and no one to call — and the ways back to people

items.title: Maryam — The Palm Tree
items.why: Alone in labor, and Allah provided for her there (19:22-26)

items.title: Yunus — The Whale's Belly
items.why: Alone in three darknesses, he called — and Allah answered (21:87-88)

line: When the heart is full and you want to say it well

dua.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
dua.body: Al-hamdu lillah — all praise is for Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a morsel of food and praises Him for it, or drinks a drink and praises Him for it. And Allah says: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.'

items.title: The Weight of One Atom
items.why: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (99:7)

items.title: Sulayman — The Kingdom
items.why: The mightiest king asked to be enabled to be grateful (27:19)

items.title: The Upper Hand
items.why: Giving from what you have been given

line: When the tank is empty and the week won't end

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى ذِكْرِكَ وَشُكْرِكَ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ
dua.body: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well. The Prophet ﷺ told Mu'adh never to leave this after any prayer. And Allah reminds us: 'We made your sleep a means for rest.' If tiredness will not lift with rest, it is worth seeing a doctor.
dua.source: Sunan Abi Dawud 1522 (sahih per al-Albani; sahih per Darussalam); Qur'an 78:9

items.title: Built to Rest
items.why: Rest is part of how you were made; the Friday pause is a standing appointment

items.title: The Birds Leave Hungry
items.why: Tawakkul is not sitting still: the birds go out in the morning

items.title: Before Sleep — Ayat al-Kursi
items.why: The Prophet ﷺ taught Ayat al-Kursi at bedtime: a guardian from Allah stays over you (Bukhari 2311)

line: When the dark gets loud

dua.arabic: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ، قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ، قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ
dua.body: Every night when he went to bed, the Prophet ﷺ would cup his hands together, blow into them after reciting al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas, and wipe over whatever he could of his body, starting with his head and face — three times.

items.title: Protection from the Jinn
items.why: A few short daily habits of protection, rather than hours of fear

items.title: Ibrahim — The Fire That Cooled
items.why: 'O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham' (21:69)

items.title: The Hijrah — The Second of Two
items.why: 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us' — said in the cave while Quraysh searched (9:40)

line: When you did the thing and the shame is loud

dua.arabic: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ
dua.body: I ask forgiveness of Allah, there is no deity but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer, and I turn to Him in repentance. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever says this is forgiven, even if he fled from the battlefield. And Allah says: do not despair of His mercy (39:53).
dua.source: Sunan Abi Dawud 1517 (sahih per al-Albani; hasan per Darussalam); Qur'an 39:53

items.title: Adam — The First Repentance
items.why: He asked forgiveness and Allah accepted his repentance (2:37; 7:23)

items.title: The Man Who Killed 99
items.why: Even after ninety-nine, repentance was accepted (Bukhari 3470)

items.title: The Prostitute's Thirst
items.why: Allah forgave her for giving water to a thirsty dog (Bukhari 3467)

line: When something good is coming and you can feel it

dua.arabic: حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
dua.body: Sufficient for us is Allah, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs. Ibrahim ﷺ said it when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad ﷺ said it when people warned that an army had gathered against them (Bukhari 4563). Allah says that they returned with favor from Allah and bounty, no harm having touched them (3:174).

items.title: Taif — Praying for Your Enemies' Grandchildren
items.why: Offered the mountains to crush the city, he hoped for their descendants instead (Bukhari 3231)

items.title: Hudaybiyyah — The Clear Conquest
items.why: A treaty that troubled even Umar — and Allah called it 'a clear conquest' (48:1)

items.title: The Beautiful Patience
items.why: 'Despair not of relief from Allah' (12:87)

line: When the map is gone and every road looks the same

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَٰذَا الْأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي
dua.body: The Prophet ﷺ taught the istikhara prayer for decisions, as he taught the surahs of the Qur'an: pray two rak'ahs other than the obligatory prayer, then say: O Allah, if You know this matter to be good for me in my religion, my livelihood and the consequence of my affairs, then decree it for me and ease it for me; and if You know it to be bad for me, turn it away from me and me away from it, and decree for me the good wherever it is.

items.title: Ibrahim — The Seeker
items.why: He looked honestly — star, moon, sun — until he found the One who does not set (6:76-79)

items.title: Solitude Is a Room
items.why: A quiet hour to listen; the Prophet ﷺ sought seclusion in Hira (Bukhari 3)

line: When the heart is quiet and you want to keep it

dua.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْهُدَىٰ وَالتُّقَىٰ وَالْعَفَافَ وَالْغِنَىٰ
dua.body: O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity and self-sufficiency. The Prophet ﷺ used to make this supplication.

items.title: Solitude Is a Room
items.why: Protect the quiet — it can be part of the deen, not an escape from it

items.title: Built to Rest
items.why: Rest is part of how you were made; keep the appointment

items.title: The Three Men in the Cave
items.why: Each prayed by an honest deed, and the rock moved (Bukhari 2215)

line: When everything is due and there is only one of you

dua.arabic: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الْأَرْضِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ
dua.body: The Prophet ﷺ used to say at times of distress: There is no deity but Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing. There is no deity but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no deity but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne.

items.title: Built to Rest
items.why: Even trade pauses for the call to Friday prayer (62:9)

items.title: The Birds Leave Hungry
items.why: Do the morning's work and trust the rest to Allah

items.title: Before Sleep — Ayat al-Kursi
items.why: A guardian from Allah stays over you through the night (Bukhari 2311)

line: When someone you trusted broke the trust

dua.arabic: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مَخْرَجًا
dua.body: And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect.

items.title: Yusuf — 'No Blame Upon You'
items.why: Betrayed by his own brothers, he said at the end: 'No blame will there be upon you today' (12:92)

items.title: Taif — Praying for Your Enemies' Grandchildren
items.why: Turned away by the city he went to for help, and he prayed for their descendants

items.title: The Beautiful Patience
items.why: Lied to by his own sons, Ya'qub said: 'patience is most fitting' (12:18)

line: When someone else's blessing stings

dua.arabic: أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ النَّاسَ عَلَىٰ مَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ
dua.body: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. And ask Allah of His bounty.

items.title: The Birds Leave Hungry
items.why: Provision is from Allah: go out in the morning and trust

items.title: The Weight of One Atom
items.why: Small unseen good is not lost (99:7)

items.title: Sulayman — The Kingdom
items.why: With a kingdom no one else would have, he asked to be grateful (27:19)

line: When nothing reaches you, not even the pain

dua.arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا ۝ إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
dua.body: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. If you have felt little or nothing for weeks, please talk to a doctor or a counselor; asking for help is not a failure of faith.

items.title: Ayyub — The Patient One
items.why: Years of affliction, then a dua, and a spring opened (38:41-42)

items.title: The Morning Remembrance
items.why: A few words on waking — a small place to start

items.title: Yunus — The Whale's Belly
items.why: From the darknesses he called, and Allah saved him (21:87-88)

line: When the heart will not sit down

dua.arabic: أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ
dua.body: Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.

items.title: Before Sleep — Ayat al-Kursi
items.why: A bedtime routine the Prophet ﷺ taught (Bukhari 2311)

items.title: Solitude Is a Room
items.why: A quiet hour as part of the deen, not an escape from it

items.title: The Two Rivers of Ibrahim
items.why: He searched honestly until he found the truth (6:76-79)

line: When you measure yourself and come up short

dua.arabic: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
dua.body: And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him.

items.title: Maryam — The Palm Tree
items.why: Questioned by her people, she pointed to the baby, and he spoke (19:27-30)

items.title: Musa — Asking for Help
items.why: He asked Allah to ease his task and to give him his brother as support (20:25-32)

items.title: Anxiety and the Reframing of Ta'weel
items.why: A reflection for the 3am ceiling

line: When the absence has a shape and a weight

dua.arabic: الَّذِينَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَالُوا إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ
dua.body: Who, when disaster strikes them, say: Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return. Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And when his son Ibrahim was dying, the Prophet ﷺ wept and said: the eyes shed tears and the heart is grieved, and we say only what pleases our Lord.

items.title: The Grammar of Loss
items.why: The words to say when loss strikes (2:156)

items.title: Umm Salama — The Dua and What Followed
items.why: She said this dua after Abu Salama died (Muslim 918)

items.title: The Beautiful Patience
items.why: Years of grief for Yusuf, and he never gave up hope in Allah (12:87)

line: When the door you prayed for closed

dua.arabic: وَعَسَىٰ أَن تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ
dua.body: But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not.

items.title: Hudaybiyyah — The Clear Conquest
items.why: A treaty that troubled the Companions — and Allah called it 'a clear conquest' (48:1)

items.title: Yusuf — From the Well to the Throne
items.why: From the well and the prison to a place of trust, after years of waiting

items.title: The Beautiful Patience
items.why: Lost Yusuf, then Binyamin — and still 'despair not of relief from Allah' (12:87)

line: When the heart lifts and you want to act on it

dua.arabic: وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا
dua.body: And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.

items.title: Musa — The Call at the Fire
items.why: He asked: 'My Lord, expand for me my breast and ease for me my task' (20:25-26)

items.title: Day 1: The Shahada — Your Door
items.why: Where the journey in this deen begins

items.title: Taif — Praying for Your Enemies' Grandchildren
items.why: Turning a painful day into hope for the future

line: When you have decided, and you need it to hold

dua.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ
dua.body: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.

items.title: The Man Who Killed 99
items.why: He set out on the road to repent and was forgiven (Bukhari 3470)

items.title: Bilal — One Word
items.why: Under torture, he answered with one word: 'Ahad, Ahad' — One, One

items.title: Nuh — The Long Building
items.why: 950 years among his people (29:14) and he kept building (11:38)

line: When what you have is enough and you know it

dua.arabic: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَرُزِقَ كَفَافًا وَقَنَّعَهُ اللَّهُ بِمَا آتَاهُ
dua.body: The Prophet ﷺ said: Successful is the one who has submitted, has been given enough, and whom Allah has made content with what He gave him.

items.title: The Weight of One Atom
items.why: Small good is not lost (99:7)

items.title: The Birds Leave Hungry
items.why: Provision is from Allah; trust and work

items.title: Sulayman — The Kingdom
items.why: The mightiest king prayed to be enabled to be grateful (27:19)

line: When the heart is broken and you are not sure it will mend

dua.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ
dua.body: And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me — indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.

items.title: Asiya — A House Near Allah
items.why: From inside Pharaoh's house she prayed: 'build for me near You a house in Paradise' (66:11)

items.title: Loneliness in the Crowd
items.why: A crowded feed and no one to call — and the ways back to people

items.title: Yunus — The Whale's Belly
items.why: From the darknesses he called, and Allah saved him (21:87-88)

line: When the past plays on a loop and you can't edit it

dua.arabic: قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِن رَّحْمَةِ اللَّهِ
dua.body: Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

items.title: Adam — The First Repentance
items.why: He asked forgiveness and Allah accepted his repentance (2:37; 7:23)

items.title: The Prostitute's Thirst
items.why: Allah forgave her for giving water to a thirsty dog (Bukhari 3467)

items.title: The Man Who Killed 99
items.why: Even after ninety-nine, repentance was accepted (Bukhari 3470)
